content: Click-events tables under high write volume should use PostgreSQL native range partitioning by time (e.g. monthly), since events are near-always queried/retained by recent time windows. Over-partitioning (daily/hourly for low-volume workloads) hurts performance more than it helps — prefer fewer, well-sized partitions (monthly is a reasonable default for a self-hosted shortener's expected scale). Partitioning also enables cheap retention/pruning by dropping old partitions instead of DELETE, and keeps indexes on the hot (current) partition small.
